body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}_{n,m}^{\mathrm{HT}},\quad R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)=D_{n,m}(\beta)+L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)\); the candidate second-order coefficients remain open.

sampling_model.design: A uniform balanced pilot split, balanced complete randomization on \(S_m\), and a pilot-measurable positive-support exact-alpha ellipsoidal mixture on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}=S_m^c\), compared with the full-array oracle on \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\).
sampling_model.units: A deterministic triangular array of \(n\) units with complete bounded baselines known before assignment and fixed realized potential outcomes for design-based inference.
sampling_model.treatment: All \(Q=2^{K_f}\) combinations receive equal wave-specific counts.
sampling_model.overlap: The fixed mixture weight \(\eta>0\) gives every balanced assignment positive probability and every unit--combination inclusion positive probability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on the selected pilot identities and balanced labels, only the revealed outcomes contribute to the likelihood.  Their score covariance is the random matrix \(I_m^{\mathrm{pil}}\).  The current assumptions do not imply convergence of this matrix to \(I(\beta)\), so nuisance-efficient estimation and its transfer to exact action loss are conditional proof goals rather than established features.

Its deterministic compact-localization and argmin-transfer architecture informs the conditional balanced-grid proposition; its binary-arm statistical rate is not transferred.
The two-stage Bayesian rerandomization procedure learns covariate importance from a pilot and improves first-order precision.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Inverse inclusion weighting gives unbiased estimation under unequal-probability sampling without replacement.
The Horvitz--Thompson estimator is quadratically mean consistent under broad general designs.
Finite-population random partitions obey joint central limit theorems for multiple treatments and vector outcomes.
Fixed symmetric factorial rerandomization yields a truncated-Gaussian joint limit and conservative confidence regions.
Finite-population Gaussian approximation supports large-sample inference for selective rerandomization but does not supply the moving-boundary second-order rate.

Quadratic-form rerandomization criteria admit fixed-geometry precision comparisons and a minimax Euclidean choice.

body.tldr: A balanced pilot and a positive-support exact-\(\alpha\) main-wave mixture retain exact Horvitz--Thompson centering for the realized finite-population factorial vector. The proved contribution includes the exact two-component risk identity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain limit, and first-order Gaussian lower-tail optimality against every admissible finite-score rule. The two proved branches rule out a fixed nondegenerate wave split and a sublinear main wave. The deterministic balanced-grid result remains conditional: compact-window second-order convergence, the pilot-information bridge, and three boundary regimes remain open, so no square-root pilot recommendation is yet certified.

project_justification.gap: Existing factorial rerandomization theory supplies first-order Gaussian precision and existing two-wave work supplies accounting architecture, but neither proves the moving-boundary exact Horvitz--Thompson comparison at the square-root pilot scale. The present information audit also shows that the stated moment conditions do not identify the pilot Fisher-information limit.
project_justification.niche: On a fixed complete baseline array with a full-dimensional product parameter domain, the design problem separates exactly into a deletion contrast and a potentially signed action-loss contrast. A compactness, leave-one-unit, and Gaussian lower-tail argument controls the latter at first order for every admissible finite-score rule, while the uniform deletion identity handles nonconvergent pilot fractions whenever the main wave diverges.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact pooled Horvitz--Thompson accounting, the explicit first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain coefficient, first-order Gaussian lower-tail optimality against every admissible finite-score rule, both macroscopic exclusion branches, the exact pilot likelihood and realized-information audit, and a conditional deterministic grid-transfer certificate. It leaves both frontier coefficients, compact-window convergence, the information-to-action bridge, and the three remaining boundary comparisons as explicit open questions.

body.related_work: Han and Deng provide the closest factorial sample-splitting architecture and first-order oracle equivalence; their results inform the present first-order comparison but do not supply the deletion cancellation or exact moving-boundary action loss.  Li and Ding provide the random-partition central limit theorem used for bounded conditional-mean tables.  Li, Ding, and Rubin provide the symmetric truncated-Gaussian predecessor, while the present first-order arbitrary-action comparison additionally carries randomized ties, exact unequal inclusions, and arbitrary centered quadratic actions through a subsequence limit.  Yamin provides the deterministic compact-localization and argmin-transfer architecture, not the statistical square-root rate or its coefficients.  Armstrong's LAN efficiency bounds become relevant only after an actual pilot-information limit is available.  Horvitz and Thompson support exact inverse-inclusion centering.  Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella motivate sequential factorial replications, but no pilot-size recommendation is certified until the compact-window and three remaining endpoint premises are proved.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Discrete score supports can create exact ties, and induced designs can have unequal inclusion probabilities. Compact rule and parameter subsequences, zero Gaussian boundary mass, an explicit leave-one-unit coupling, and exact residual cancellation absorb those effects only at first order. They do not provide an \(n^{-3/2}\) remainder, so they do not establish the compact-window second-order premise or the three remaining boundary comparisons. Separately, smooth first and second outcome moments do not control score information as a function of the baseline, so the pilot LAN information cannot be fixed at \(I(\beta)\) without additional derivation.
body.honest_scope: Established results are exact Horvitz--Thompson centering and accounting, the one-wave risk bound, common oracle-map convergence, Gaussian boundary regularity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle gain, first-order Gaussian lower-tail optimality against every admissible finite-score rule, the exact pilot likelihood and information audit, the two proved macroscopic exclusions covering fixed nondegenerate wave splits and sublinear main waves, and the conditional deterministic grid transfer. The coefficient \(A\) remains an unresolved deletion candidate and \(B\) remains a Gaussian action candidate. Uniform frontier-scale deletion, exact finite action curvature, information convergence, bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), the regime \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\), and the unconditional global pilot rule are open. The causal estimand remains the fixed realized factorial vector throughout.
body.interpretation: For planning, the proved coefficient \(a(\beta)\) quantifies the first-order loss from deleting a macroscopic fraction of units for learning.  No exact finite quadratic action can asymptotically beat the empirical Gaussian oracle at order \(N^{-1}\), even though finite-lattice action-loss contrasts may be negative.  Consequently, the second branch of the endpoint lemma rules out pilot and main waves that both retain positive fractions, while its first branch rules out a sublinear main wave.  The familiar balance \(A t+B/t\) remains a conditional design calculation, not a validated sample-size rule for this experiment.
